x-improve review of all 14 incident samples, 2026-10-21

Scope
Seven original, SHA-256-verified wheels; the original source distribution;
three injected files in both Unix and Windows byte variants. Existing bad-pool
labels are retained, including the source archive and the two import-only .pth
files. Payloads were read and decoded statically; none was executed.

Corrections
- Windows CNG's ctypes.windll.bcrypt is not the bcrypt password hash. Python
  password-hashing evidence now requires its bcrypt API or import; other
  language/reference spellings and the public bcrypt consumer ID are retained.
- Username/hostname queries, Base64 and an HTTP client are a neutral HTTP
  context, not proof of system-information exfiltration.
- SSH-directory listings are neutral filesystem observations. Listing and
  nearby upload code do not bind any private-key bytes to a request body.
  Rebased exact package composites still require their other read/upload legs.
- Neutral cloud metadata endpoint groups, rclone.conf references and decoded
  .exe paths moved out of credential-theft/exfiltration/dropper classifications.
  The decoded executable path matcher never required PowerShell.
- Architecture assignment plus a host query does not prove build selection.
- Large encoded execution alone is suspicious concealment, not a hostile
  verdict. Both medium and large Base64-exec rules retain their matchers.
- Descriptions of encoded Python primitives and multi-store credential targets
  now state the actual observations instead of asserting unproven data flow.

Precision and new coverage
The two proximity-based environment credential filters were replaced by one
structural matcher. It joins the environment key to the positive credential
condition, including case conversion, prefixes/suffixes, inline any() terms and
locally bound pattern lists. Truthy value filters, filtering a different value,
negation, exclusions and an unrelated nearby credential word are insufficient.
The two vocabulary components used only by the retired filters were removed.
The two existing hostile corpus cases using any() continue to be detected.

Python AES-CBC construction now requires AES and CBC origins on the two arguments
of the same Cipher call. A separate AES-GCM call and non-AES CBC call cannot
jointly satisfy it. Both import alias variants and actual payloads are covered.
Quoted SQL now exposes references to LiteLLM provider-credential/model tables.
These remain notable references; existing query-call rules separately establish
that SQL reaches a database API. A schema/table name alone is insufficient.

Consumer and taxonomy audit
Fourteen traits were relocated. Matchers and effective file
and platform scopes are retained for these moves; IDs, descriptions and levels
now reflect the observations. Direct consumers were rebased. Broad objective
selectors intentionally stop receiving moved neutral context as credential
acquisition or exfiltration evidence, or as an exception to independent theft.
This is a precision correction, not an implicit preservation of a false claim.
The filesystem listing directory stays at its budget by consolidating the two
same-scope CRT enumeration API variants and the two same-scope directory method
name strings. Their consumers used alternatives; references were consolidated
without turning either API into an additional evidence role.

Validation
check-improve.py creates inert temporary controls and can also inspect the six
verified payload files and two decoded bodies. No samples are imported.
Commands, counts, per-sample results and limitations are recorded below after the
final atomscan pass.

Final verification
- atomscan --no-update --mode slow --follow=none --rizin-timeout-secs 60
  --format=json was run for every exact input hash with the local traits tree.
- All 14 final reports use revision we4d617ec6569c7fa. Input hashes matched their
  report roots. Import-only .pth files and the payload-free sdist remain 0/0;
  they retain their user-directed bad labels.
- Each wheel: 8 hostile/9 suspicious -> 5 hostile/8 suspicious.
- Each cook.py: 5 hostile/7 suspicious -> 2 hostile/6 suspicious.
- Each sitecustomize.py: 4 hostile/6 suspicious -> 4 hostile/5 suspicious.
- New AES-CBC and both SQL table-reference facts occur in all four Python
  payload variants. Retired overclaiming IDs are absent. No suspicious/hostile
  finding appeared in any other wheel member.
- 46 focused controls passed, including all six payload files, both decoded
  bodies, a collector with changed campaign markers/domain/helper names, and a
  startup backdoor with renamed callbacks. Both variants retain their generic
  hostile detections. Quoted/mutated programs were never executed.
- make validate passed every fixture suite, including hostile 759/759, benign
  1785/1785, does-nothing 176/176, drop-exec 45/45 and supply-chain-corpus 555/555.
- git diff --check passed.

Reproduce focused controls from this repository:
python3 testdata/litellm-safedep/check-improve.py
python3 testdata/litellm-safedep/check-improve.py --sample-root /tmp/triage/litellm-safedep

Limitations
These are static observations, not observed runtime effects. The reports expose
flow-graph-limited, flow-query-incomplete, flow-call-unavailable and
flow-field-unavailable limitations.
The renamed-payload checks establish resilience to those mutations, not every
possible transformation. The unrecovered remote codepy stage remains unknown.
Raw reports and logs are under /tmp/triage/litellm-safedep/improve/; samples and
full raw reports are not copied into this repository.

Hopper read-back and Lab publication check
Direct fresh reads confirmed all 14 hashes carry we4d617ec6569c7fa and the final hostile/suspicious counts. Twelve match the standalone ML and primary findings exactly; Unix cook.pth and sitecustomize.py retain same-revision wheel-member reports. Hopper declined their standalone renewals as current. Unix cook.py had been replaced by a later old-rule worker report and was renewed with the final local result.
At this earlier check, all 14 stored envelopes lacked an LLM interpretation. The Prism Fallout homepage additionally requires a nonempty why and hostile LLM grade. These static/ML uploads therefore do not establish publication eligibility; the missing interpretation pass was not included in the scan commands.

LLM-enabled rerun and publication verification
At the user request, all 14 exact samples were rescanned with --llm http://interpret:8000/v1 and uploaded through SCAN_HOPPER. The LLM probability gate and benign notable cap were disabled for this run, so every requested sample received an actual interpretation. The service selected Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B. Current local rules had advanced to revision 4ce95; no rule edits were made for this rerun.
Fresh Hopper read-backs matched all 14 local ML and LLM results exactly. LLM grades: 11 hostile (seven original wheels plus four Python payloads), two suspicious (.pth imports), one benign (payload-free source archive). User-directed bad labels are retained for every sample.
After one explicit hard-refresh read rebuilt the Lab cache, the public /fallout.json contained all seven original wheel hashes as hostile with hostile LLM grades, and the homepage contained LiteLLM.
